headline: COPPER LME SQUEEZE BREAKS: $545/T Backwardation Collapses To $248/T After Trafigura Delivers 20,000 Tons
snippet: Trafigura Group and other traders placed more than 20,000 tonnes of copper on warrant in a single day — the largest single-day LME warehouse gain since April — collapsing the cash-to-three-month backwardation from $545/tonne (widest since the 2021 LME crisis) to $248/tonne on Tuesday. The extraordinary squeeze had built as US copper imports ran at a 12-year high after tariff front-running drained LME available stocks 14% since late July. For retail investors: the backwardation collapse signals short-term relief in the physical delivery market, but the structural copper deficit thesis — Grasberg force majeure, Kamoa-Kakula flooding, and electrification demand — remains firmly intact. The squeeze mechanics are unwinding; the fundamentals are not.

headline: URANIUM MINERS' BEST AUGUST IN YEARS: Sector Index +17%, Junior Miners +21.75%, Spot Hits $89.50/lb
snippet: HANetf's Uranium Miners Monthly Report for August 2026 documents the sector's strongest August performance in recent years: the Northshore Global Uranium Mining Index rose 17.01% and junior uranium miners gained 21.75% for the month. Spot uranium hit US$89.50/lb, a new six-month high, with term prices moving in parallel. Supply constraints deepened with Kazatomprom's TQZ sulphuric acid plant facing additional delays — construction halted after workers discovered palaeontological specimens at the site — adding fresh uncertainty to Kazakh output projections that had already been revised lower. US utilities remain roughly 30% contracted against their 10-year requirements, far below the historical 70–80% norm.

headline: NEVGOLD FORMALIZES FIRST U.S. ANTIMONY-GOLD OXIDE MRE — 15.2Mt M&I At 0.37 g/t AuEq + 31,800T Sb, NI 43-101 Filed
snippet: NevGold Corp. (TSX-V: NAU; OTC: NAUFF) filed the NI 43-101 Technical Report on August 31, 2026, formalising the Mineral Resource Estimate for its Limousine Butte gold-antimony project in Elko County, Nevada. Measured and Indicated resources stand at 15.2 million tonnes at 0.37 g/t gold-equivalent, containing 181,400 oz gold and 31,800 tonnes of antimony; Inferred adds 117.5 million tonnes with a further 75,700 tonnes of antimony. The first three holes of the 2026 20,000-metre drill program have already pushed mineralization 100+ metres beyond the current block model boundaries, with 25 holes awaiting assays. Antimony is a U.S. critical mineral and Chinese export restrictions have significantly tightened available Western supply in 2026.

headline: BLUE JAY GOLD DRILLS YUKON ANTIMONY — 10-Hole Becker-Cochran Program Starts; Skukum Gold-Silver Assays Due September
snippet: Blue Jay Gold Corp. (TSX-V: JAY) announced August 31, 2026, the commencement of a 10-hole diamond drill program at the Becker-Cochran Antimony Occurrence on its Steller Gold Project in southern Yukon. The underground workings halted in the 1960s when antimony prices collapsed — not due to resource depletion — making this structure a historically unfinished target reopened by today's critical mineral pricing environment. Metallurgical studies on 400+ kg of stibnite-rich core are underway at ALS Kamloops, results expected later in September. The company also expects to release assay results from its 2026 gold-silver drill program at the Skukum Creek and Mt. Skukum deposits in September.

headline: BANK OF AMERICA HOLDS $130/LB URANIUM TARGET FOR 2027 — Cameco's 10M-Lb Production Gap Is The Real Market Warning
snippet: The Oregon Group's analysis of Bank of America's latest uranium research finds the bank maintaining its $130/lb uranium price target for 2027 — a 52% premium to current spot — even after lowering its Cameco price objective 5% following Q2 2026 results. The structural argument: Cameco expects to mine only 19.5–21.5 million pounds in 2026 while committing to deliver 29–32 million pounds, bridging the gap through inventory draws and purchased uranium. This production-versus-delivery gap is the mechanism by which spot deficits become term contract premiums, and BofA sees this pattern accelerating through 2027 as utility undercontracting forces higher prices.

headline: MINING STOCKS 'GENERATIONAL VALUE' CASE: Gold 60%+ YoY, Equities Still At Historic Discount To Underlying Metal
snippet: A GoldSeek analysis argues that gold and silver mining stocks remain at a historically unprecedented discount to the underlying metals, with gold up more than 60% year-on-year and equities still not reflecting the earnings power that entails. The piece highlights that institutional allocation to gold mining equities has materially lagged the physical metal rally — a pattern that has historically corrected sharply once the broader market re-rates the sector on fundamentals rather than sentiment. The August 31 Warsh/Iran selloff is framed as creating exactly the entry conditions this thesis describes: forced liquidation of speculative longs at a time when underlying free cash flow generation is at record levels.

headline: CANADA MINING M&A AT DECADE HIGH — Global Deal Volume Up 45% As Majors Scramble For Copper, Gold And Battery Metal Reserves
snippet: Mining M&A drove Canada's deal market to its highest level in a decade through mid-2026, with global mining transactions above US$500 million rising approximately 45% versus 2025. Analysts attribute the surge to major producers urgently needing to replenish copper, gold, and battery metal reserves as organic exploration has failed to pace depleting existing mines. Landmark deals include Agnico Eagle's completed Rupert Resources arrangement, Hudbay's Arizona Sonoran acquisition creating the third-largest copper district in North America, and multiple Athabasca Basin uranium consolidations. Analysts expect deal flow to accelerate through Q4 as BHP, Rio Tinto, and Glencore have all signalled increased M&A appetite.

headline: AFTER THE WARSH SELL-OFF: Gold Vs Silver Mining Stocks — Which Has The Higher Return Potential From Here?
snippet: Canadian Mining Report's post-selloff analysis compares gold and silver mining equities following the August 31 drop triggered by Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks. The analysis notes that silver mining stocks carry asymmetric leverage to a silver price recovery relative to physical silver, given operating cost structures that amplify price moves. At current silver prices ($66+), producers with sub-$15/oz AISC are generating margins well above historical norms. Any reversal of the post-Warsh widening of the gold-silver ratio has historically signalled the beginning of a sharp silver equity recovery phase — the piece makes the case that junior silver developers offer the highest risk-adjusted upside in the current environment.

headline: MONEY METALS: HOW TO POSITION IN SILVER IN 2026 — Sixth Deficit, Three Risk Profiles, And The China Export Licence Trigger
snippet: Money Metals Exchange's 2026 silver investment guide outlines a framework for retail investors navigating the sixth consecutive silver supply deficit. The analysis covers three risk profiles: physical silver (no counterparty risk, direct commodity exposure), silver royalty and streaming companies (lower volatility, dividend potential), and junior silver explorers and developers (high leverage, high risk). Key metrics to watch include the gold-silver ratio (silver historically outperforms when the ratio contracts below 70:1), COMEX and LBMA exchange stocks (declining inventories signal tightening physical supply), and China's 44-firm silver export licence system — any reduction in approved exporters would be a sharp near-term price catalyst.

headline: WESTERN RARE EARTH SUPPLY CHAIN 2026: Project Vault, Serra Verde Financing, And The Magnet Manufacturing Chokepoint
snippet: Rare Earth Exchanges maps the Western rare earth supply chain's 2026 progress and remaining structural gaps. On the positive side: the White House's $12 billion Project Vault Critical Minerals Reserve, USA Rare Earth securing $1.55 billion in Serra Verde financing with government-backed terbium ($2,050/kg) and dysprosium ($575/kg) price floors, and Lynas Rare Earths posting record FY2026 revenue of A$977.9 million with a new 10-year Malaysian operating licence. The persistent chokepoint: China still processes approximately 94% of all rare earth-based magnets globally. The analysis names magnet manufacturing — not mining or separation — as the last and most difficult link for the West to close in building a genuinely independent rare earth supply chain.
